YOUR NEXT STEP, PREPARED

Bring your curiosity.
And your favorite AI.

01

Shortlist and watch.

Save promising projects and issues with private notes. Watch an issue and get a notification when it is unassigned, gets a pull request, a claim goes quiet or it closes.

02

Summarize on your device.

Long thread? Chrome’s built-in AI summarizes it and suggests first steps — locally, without uploading anything. Other browsers show the latest comments at a glance, no AI needed.

03

Or bring your favorite AI.

Copy a source-linked contribution brief into ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Nothing is sent automatically.

A FEW FIELD NOTES

Good questions.
Clear answers.

Is CONTRI free?+

Yes. The source is available under the MIT license. You can inspect it, improve it, and build on it.

Do I need to sign in?+

No. Anonymous mode works within GitHub’s limit of 60 requests an hour. Signing in with GitHub (read-only, no scopes) raises it to 5,000 and makes most checks a single request. Your sign-in is forgotten when the browser closes unless you choose otherwise, and it is only ever sent to GitHub.

How does it know who the maintainers are?+

From public evidence: GitHub’s team badges, who labels, assigns and merges, CODEOWNERS and the repository owner. That finds maintainers GitHub hides as “contributors”, but it is still not a complete roster, and every result explains its coverage.

Does “Looks free” mean nobody is working on it?+

Not quite. It means CONTRI found no assignee, no recent “I’d like to work on this” claim and no linked open pull request. Someone may still be working quietly, so say hello in the thread before you start.

Does CONTRI need AI to work?+

No. Badges, claims, linked pull requests, reply times and activity are plain rules over public GitHub data, and work the same in Chrome, Edge and Brave. AI is only two optional buttons that use the model built into your browser, on your device; where there is none, CONTRI shows the latest comments instead.

What stays on my device?+

Cached public reports, your shortlist and notes, watched issues, preferences and, if you choose, your sign-in. AI summaries run on your device with Chrome’s built-in model. There is no analytics or backend. The full privacy policy is in the repository.

Is it on the Chrome Web Store?+

Yes. Install CONTRI from the Chrome Web Store in one click. The same listing works in Edge and Brave, and an experimental Firefox build is on GitHub.

Star CONTRI
  1. Open CONTRI on the Chrome Web Store and click Add to Chrome. In Edge, allow extensions from other stores when asked.
  2. A welcome page opens — sign in with GitHub, or just close it to use CONTRI without an account.
  3. Open any public repository and look for the compass button and the badge under issue titles.

Chrome, Edge or Brave 124+. For Firefox or a manual install, download the contri-v….zip from the latest release and follow the README.
